title: Lorenzo Staulz, uptown guitarist and close friend
summary: St. Cyr discusses the spelling of Lorenzo Staulz's name, his brothers, his guitar playing, friendship with St. Cyr, and where he lived and worked.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: Speaking of uptown fellows, what about Lorenzo Stahl? Did he take Brock's place? Was he a little younger than Brock or did he?
Well, yeah, he was younger than Brock. I mean, he'd taken Brock's place.
Oh, do you know that his last name, is it spelled, you know how it's spelled or pronounced exactly, is it Stahl or some people say Star, like the star up in the sky?
No, no, no, it's not like Star in the sky. It's, I think it's S-T-A-W-L-S. Stahls. Stahls.
Somebody said it might have a Z in. That sounds something like the way you said it.

No, no, it's not no Z. No Z. No, not Stahls. It's Stahls. It's T-A-W-L-S. I think that's what it's spelled. I never find it. I looked at it. Yeah, there's a brother out here by the name of Stanley Stahl.
Yeah. Oh gee, I could stay a month out here and not meet everybody.
Stanley's a bricklayer, but he had another brother by the name of Sidney Stahl, but he died. He was a blast truck. But Stanley's still living, I think, he's still out here.

Yeah, well, Lorenzo was a bricklayer, but he had another brother by the name of Sidney Stahls, but he died. He was a blast truck. But Stanley's still living, I think, he's still out here. Yeah, well, Lorenzo was one of the best guitar players we had uptown.

Was he really a good guitar player? Yeah, he was a good guitar player. Well, you used to sing some of these songs at Fest and I was a little while. Yeah, yeah, yeah, a little while. You think he was mostly an entertainer or he was really a good musician? Yes, he was. A good guitar player.
Yeah, he's a great guy. He was a very good friend of mine. Very good friend of mine. We were like brothers. And where did you live about him? He lived at Leotin and Pitt.
Oh, right out there? Yeah, right out there.
A block above St. Charles and one block below Peters Avenue, which is now Jefferson Davis.
He had a presser by trade. He had a cleaning and pressing establishment.
